six horrs thrpugh five suecessive days. There was no respite. The mucceeding weak commenced the actual term. We had askad the appointmant of one men among the meny taschers, on to whose shoulders could be shifted the heaviest burdens, if desired. I comenced on Monday with a hoarse, tired voice, something I had never know. In spite of all palliatives, uttemnca grew weaker and nore diffionlt, and finally ceased. The other teachers, and my own splendid pupils came tenderly to my aid reliaving me of avery duty possible to be done. To assure the proper arrangements and management of the school in its beginning, I hopefully ranainad for sone weeks at my voicalese post, but it was a vain affort. I bagan to realise that the weakining wes not entirely confined to the voice. The labore of the past months had not been a pastime for either weel? or my inveluable helpmeet, and in the midst of protests, loyal and loving, our resignetions were given. We could searcely say they wars gecepted.

I have selected one letter from among my Grand Aunts papers to show

With what affectin are joy she look back on the old school days

in Bordentown.

I have soarched through the sarliest diaries we have and find thie little entry on the fly leaf;- Oct. 15/61 Left hone for It. (Hightatorn) Oet. 23 Thursday. Commenced school. Attonded a weakly st

Ire. Tailore in the evening.

May 27 / 5%.

And in the back of the same little diary I find Arrived in Bordentow.

Immediately following thie lible entry is a tiet of "Poats From Chaucer to the presont day, " which fill up some ter or twalve pages of the

little book.
